If possible, please attach any simple diagrams and a single-sheet matrix we can include in the board packet. We are on a tight timeline and would like a response by end of day Wednesday PT.

The attack-matrix summary is attached as a PDF (one page per vector). High level notes inline below; the attachments contain the formal write-ups you can include in the packet.

High-level answers:
- Egress chronology: outbound connections originate from the inference runtime process -> routed through a tenant sidecar proxy -> evaluated by local egress policy (whitelist + dynamic token exchange) -> forwarded to regional outbound gateway which enforces cloud-provider-level network policies and customer-specific allowlists. During fallback (eg, model substitution or fail-open) the runtime flips to a read-only cache mode and sidecar blocks all new external destinations except metrics/tracing endpoints and our signed failover control plane.
- Attack matrix brief: see attack_matrix_summary.pdf for the one-paragraph entries. In short, risk modelling assumes an externally-exposed control plane is 1) guarded by mutual TLS + mTLS to regional controllers, 2) every sensitive action requires an ops-signed token with TTL and audit hooks, and 3) tenant KV separation + encrypted-at-rest model shards reduce data exposure windows.

We have a few internal SMEs I want to loop in to validate wording for the board packet — copying Vanessa (network architect) and Neha (security compliance) for quick confirmation. If Wednesday EOD PT is still the ask, we can finalize and send a polished packet by then.

Michael — quick checks below, pulled from the diagram and our runbook language. I kept each item to one sentence for inclusion in the packet.

1) Egress chronology (network side):
- Normal op: Inference runtime opens sockets to localhost sidecar (no direct host egress). Sidecar authenticates the request using per-tenant TLS cert and consults the local policy engine (policy version pinned per-rollout) before initiating outbound connections to the regional gateway.
- Gateway enforcement: Regional gateway enforces cloud-provider SG/NACL policies and our managed allowlists; any destination outside allowlist is dropped and audited.
- Fallback behaviors: On model failover or control-plane unreachability, sidecar transitions to strict-block (metrics + control plane heartbeats only) and all dynamic outbound tokens are revoked immediately via short-lived token introspection.

2) Control-plane (Neha can expand on ops controls) short line for likelihood:
- Likelihood: control-plane compromise is modelled as low (threat requires chained credential exposure); mitigations include mTLS, aggressive rotation, and contractor-requirement approvals.

3) Neighbor-tenant escape (attack surface):
- Risk: negligible-to-low under normal configs because tenant memory and KV namespaces are strongly isolated; sidecar enforces namespace-scoped caches and the runtime uses address-space randomization plus kernel namespaces per tenant.

4) Sidecar chaining / supply-chain vectors (one sentence each):
- Sidecar chaining: chaining requires successful payload injection into sidecar or escalation from container runtime — our build pipeline signs sidecar images and runtime verifies signatures at startup.
- Supply chain: we assume third-party model artifacts are signed; ingestion rejects unsigned artifacts and we run malware scanning and model checksum attestation before deployment.

Suggested additions for the attack-matrix wording: short likelihood assumptions are "low (requires privileged access)", "medium (exploits unpatched packages)", "low (requires strong supply-chain failure)" mapped to vectors respectively.

I'll sign off if Neha confirms the ops token revocation phrasing.

—Vanessa
Network Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Alejandra / Tom —

Thanks for the request and for the quick turnaround window. Attached please find a concise packet you can include in the vendor board:
- redwood_network_diagram_v3.png — annotated network topology (runtime, sidecar, regional gateway, control plane) with numbered egress hops for the chronology.
- isolation_matrix_v1.xlsx — single-sheet matrix showing tenancy boundaries, KV separation, memory isolation, and policy enforcement points.
- attack_matrix_summary.pdf — one-paragraph risk/likelihood/control mappings for the vectors you listed (control plane compromise, neighbor-tenant escape, sidecar chaining, supply-chain compromise).

Key excerpts you can lift directly into your packet:
- Egress chronology (summary):
  1) Runtime → Local sidecar (mutual TLS, tenant-scoped cert)
  2) Sidecar policy evaluation (whitelist + dynamic token exchange)
  3) Regional outbound gateway (cloud SG/NACL + managed allowlist)
  4) External destination (only allowed destinations per-customer)
  Fallback: on control-plane loss or failover conditions the sidecar revokes new token issuance and enforces strict-block mode (metrics and signed-control-heartbeats only).

- Attack-matrix summary (very brief):
  • Control plane compromise — Likelihood: low. Controls: mTLS, short-lived ops tokens, multi-person approval for critical actions, continuous audit + incident playbooks.
  • Neighbor-tenant escape — Likelihood: low. Controls: namespace-scoped caches, KV encryption, runtime memory isolation, automated tenant attestation tests during deployments.
  • Sidecar chaining — Likelihood: medium. Controls: signed sidecar images, runtime bootstrap verification, image vulnerability scanning, and process-level seccomp filters.
  • Supply chain compromise — Likelihood: low-to-medium. Controls: artifact signing, checksum attestation, ingestion sandboxing, and curated model catalogs with provenance metadata.

If you'd like we can run a 30-minute walkthrough for the board next week and share the editable Diagrams/Sheets. Proposed slots: Thu Jun 24 11:00-11:30 PT or Fri Jun 25 09:00-09:30 PT. Please let me know what works.

Respectfully,
